summary: Built 1922 as a 60-ft steel lookout on the Bridgeton Pike near Millville, Cumberland County, NJ; later raised to 100 ft; a watchman staffed it until 1942.

facts.design: Steel Aermotor tower, 60 ft originally with a 7'x7' metal cab; later raised to 100 ft

events.note: Register gives 1922; the 1922-23 state annual report says it opened for service April 1
Replaced an earlier structure of local design
Watchman Josiah Hankins served from the time the tower was built
Hankins retired a few weeks before an April 20, 1942 newspaper item

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1922-23 annual report places the tower about 2 miles west of Millville; an April 26, 1922 newspaper item places it 2 1/2 miles east. The sources do not reconcile this, so the story reports both.
The annual report says it opened for service April 1, 1922; the April 26, 1922 newspaper item says it had just been opened. Not reconciled.

notes_for_editor: No source read documents current access or current staffing. The register page is undated, so 'listed as in active service' is its claim only. No specific fire found. The NJFFS fire-towers page at dep.nj.gov returned empty via fetch_text and WebFetch. The 1922 location and opening-date conflict is left open. Fact-check 2026-10-08: NHLR page confirms the agency and 2004 registration; Eastern US Lookouts confirms the April 26, 1922 and April 20, 1942 item dates and the watchman wording.
